# `assertion-free-test`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: style · Profile: none · Default: off · Fixes: none · Options: none

Reports a test block with no expectation, propagated fallible call, catch, or
debug assertion.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

An accidental assertion-free test passes when behavior is wrong and verifies
only that execution did not crash.

## When it fires

A test asserts by construction when it only references declarations so the
compiler checks them (`_ = X;` or `_ = @import(...);`, also under an `if` or a
`comptime` block), calls `refAllDecls` or `refAllDeclsRecursive`, has an empty
body (a doctest anchor such as `test name {}`), or starts with
`return error.SkipZigTest`; none of these is reported. Explicit crash-only
tests can suppress the rule, documenting that their absence of an expectation
is intentional.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
fn setup() void {}

test "setup" {
    setup();
}
```
